clue.text: Basic stuff — aluminium repeatedly split by potassium and iodine

indicators.note: split by says the doubled symbol is broken apart with the potassium symbol in the gap
repeatedly asks for the aluminium symbol to be written twice

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
K is the chemical symbol for potassium
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe for a basic compound built from aluminium, potassium and iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a base is the opposite of an acid, and a soluble base is exactly this kind of substance.

clue.text: Welsh doctor with attitude turning up in prison

indicators.note: in says the doctor and the upturned attitude go inside the prison word

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for attitude is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A Welsh medic with a bad attitude ends up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for Wales is Cambria, so the adjective means Welsh, as in the Cambrian Mountains.

clue.text: Good Dickens character showing resentment

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A kindly Dickens figure who nonetheless bears ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name lingering bitterness over a past wrong, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Resident military leader taking trophy to soldier?

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
a cup is a sporting trophy
a soldier ant is a caste of ant, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A local commander carries a prize off to one of his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in or holds a place is its occupier, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hit band in riot hurries to be displaying added security

parts.note: to belt is to hit hard

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters of band are thrown about

parts.note: races means hurries

explanation.surface: A rowdy band runs riot and rushes off in search of extra protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit band' reads as a hit record, but hit is a separate verb here; 'in riot' scrambles the band's letters to ANDB.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes taking a double precaution, like wearing both a belt and braces to hold up trousers.

clue.text: Country fellows following inclination and time to get note of available funds

indicators.note: following places the country and fellows after the inclination

parts.note: a bank is a slope or incline
a state is a country
men means fellows

explanation.surface: Rural folk go along with a trend and eventually get a note about their money.
explanation.definitionFit: The document a bank sends lists a customer's balance and transactions, showing what money is there.

clue.text: One should be gentle around gums, ultimately, when at work

definitions.text: One should be gentle around gums, ultimately, when at work

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters are busily rearranged
ultimately picks the final letter of gums

explanation.surface: Advice that someone working in mouths should take care around the gums.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of GENTLE AROUND plus S, the last letter of gums, gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes that professional.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist operating on teeth and mouths is expected to treat sensitive gum tissue gently.

clue.text: A lot of condiment taking care of sauce

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the last letter of the condiment is dropped

parts.note: salt is a condiment
addressing a problem is dealing with or taking care of it

explanation.surface: Too much seasoning goes into the making of a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinaigrette or mayonnaise poured over leaves is a kind of sauce.

clue.text: Independent with new account backing member of historic race

indicators.note: backing means the account abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An independent candidate with fresh funding supports a member of an ancient people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean empire of Peru was ruled by this people, so one of them belongs to a historic race.

clue.text: Crooked doppelgänger has you looking agonised?

parts.note: bent means crooked, physically or morally
a double is a lookalike or doppelgänger

explanation.surface: Meeting your dishonest lookalike leaves you wincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone folded over in pain looks agonised; the question mark admits this is a description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Aid reduced to Italy and city there

indicators.note: reduced means the help word loses its final letter

parts.note: to assist is to aid
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Aid to Italy is cut back, and one of its cities suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hill town in Umbria, home of St Francis, is a city in Italy, which 'there' points back to.

clue.text: Woman American called back when in A&E

indicators.note: when in places the reversed word inside the hospital department letters

parts.note: the letters A and E as printed

indicators.note: back means the phoning word is read in reverse

parts.note: dialed is the American spelling for telephoned

explanation.surface: A woman phones an American while waiting in casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department. 'back' turns DIALED into DELAID.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's first name, also a city in South Australia.

clue.text: Transmit radio waves one controls

indicators.note: waves suggests the letters undulate and move about

explanation.surface: A broadcasting instruction: send radio waves out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' looks like the object of transmit, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager or controller runs an organisation's affairs, so this person is one who controls.

clue.text: Contents of some altimeter may reveal when flight attendants are active

indicators.note: contents of means the letters sit inside the words some altimeter

explanation.surface: An aircraft instrument reading reveals when the cabin crew get busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin crew are busiest serving food, so the time of dining is when they are active.

clue.text: Rotting is due to pervade odd stuff left over

indicators.note: to pervade means the rearranged letters spread through the middle of the odd word

parts.note: rum is old slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: rotting means the letters of is due decay into a new order

explanation.surface: Something rotten spreading through strange leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotting' scrambles the letters of 'is due' to ESIDU; rum in the sense of odd is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for a remainder or residue, what remains after a process.

clue.text: Allegorical figure hit hard amidst ruins of Rome

indicators.note: amidst places the hit and hard letters in the middle of the ruined Rome
ruins of means the letters of Rome are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: tap means hit
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A symbolic statue struck hard among the ruins of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins of' rearranges the city's letters to MEOR, which is then split open.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech that describes one thing as another is a kind of implied comparison, like allegory in miniature.

clue.text: Roman poet's house and lineage

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the poet is the house and lineage

parts.note: a race is a line of descent or lineage

explanation.surface: A Roman poet's home and ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintus Horatius Flaccus, writer of Odes, is the famous Roman poet known by this English name.

clue.text: Evidence of visit to loo involving pee?

definitions.text: Evidence of visit to loo involving pee?

indicators.note: involving means the loo-visit word wraps around the letter

parts.note: slash is British slang for an act of urinating
pee is the spoken name of the letter P

explanation.surface: Telltale signs left behind after a trip to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: SLASH is crude British slang for a trip to urinate. The whole clue also defines the answer: spilt drops are the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Spattered droplets around a toilet are telltale marks of someone having relieved themselves carelessly.

clue.text: Something like water I found in pounds

indicators.note: found in places the letter I inside the two pound words

parts.note: L (from libra) and quid are each a pound, so pounds supplies both

explanation.surface: Discovering something watery in a stack of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds is plural, giving two words for a pound: L and QUID (British slang for a pound sterling).
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the standard example of a fluid substance that flows and takes its container's shape.

clue.text: Had to limit end of debate after landlord's identification in correspondence

indicators.note: after places the limited had following the landlord

parts.note: a landlord is one who lets property, a letter; the 's is a joining link

indicators.note: to limit means had closes around the letter from debate
end of picks the last letter of debate

explanation.surface: A landlord's letter cuts short the end of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed heading on writing paper identifies the sender of business mail.

clue.text: Showing little activity, losing energy, coming to stop

indicators.note: losing means a letter drops out of the calm word

parts.note: quiet means showing little activity
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sluggish engine, running out of energy, coasts to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or give up doing something is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Prolonged sentence given to prisoners not initially angry

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence
cons are convicts, prisoners

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the angry word goes

parts.note: fuming means angry

explanation.surface: A long jail term hands inmates who are no longer quite so furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes a long while is drawn out, protracted.
